title: Crumbtrail regression scrapbook
content:
Quick note: this is a personal scratchpad for the "crumbtrail" approach — tracking small anchor spans that seem to pull the model into hallucination over a generation. Not polished; a mixture of observations, output snippets, and short experiments to reproduce a regression we noticed in nightly runs.

Goal / hypothesis:
- Problem: a subset of long-form QA prompts end up with plausible but fabricated references (dates, paper names). The failure often emerges 40-120 tokens into the answer.
- Hypothesis: a short token span earlier in the context (5–15 tokens) acts as a trigger/anchor when combined with a specific model variant + sampling config (temp >= 0.6, top_p ~0.95).
- Approach: "crumbtrail" = 1) identify earliest token span correlated with hallucination, 2) systematically mutate that span, 3) rerun small ensembles to test sensitivity.

Ad-hoc rubric (quick, 1–4 scale for triage):
- Factual accuracy: 1 (fabricated facts) -> 4 (verifiable and cited)
- Attribution clarity: 1 (implicit fabricated citation) -> 4 (explicit source + correct link)
- Drift onset latency: measured in tokens before first hallucinated claim (smaller = worse)
- Reproducibility across seeds: FAIL / PARTIAL / PASS

Sample failing case (trimmed):
- Prompt (redacted): "Given the transcript below, summarize the key technical claims and list three related papers that validate them." + 6-paragraph transcript about agent-based simulation results.
- Model: redwood-instruct-1.2-q4 (dedicated dev pool), temp=0.7, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=512
- Output excerpt (hallucination marked):
  "The study mirrors results from "Adaptive Schedulers for Agent-based Models" (Zhou et al., 2020) which showed a 2.3x improvement in throughput. [BAD-CITE]"

Notes on the sample:
- "Adaptive Schedulers for Agent-based Models" is not in our citation corpus; quick search returns no id. Claim about 2.3x also not referenced in transcript.
- First invented phrase appears near token ~82 in generation; prior tokens were all faithful paraphrase. That suggests a latent switch around that span.

Crumbtrail trace for this case (manual):
- Step 1: isolate seed A (seed 3241) run that produced hallucination. Save token-level trace from runtime (kv cache markers + logits if available).
- Step 2: extract the 12-token window immediately before hallucination start (tokens 70-81) from the prompt+generation context.
- Step 3: mutate windows: blank out, replace with neutral phrase ("the following section"), replace with factual anchor (a real paper title), and mutate punctuation only.

Quick experiment results (notes):
- Blank-out window -> hallucination still happens but delayed ~18 tokens (onset token 100). Reproducibility: PARTIAL across seeds (3/5 runs).
- Replace with neutral phrase -> reduces halluc rate in 4/5 runs (PASS), generated related papers are generic but not fabricated.
- Replace with real paper title -> model latches on to that paper and attributes correct-ish claims to it (PASS but irrelevant attribution).
- Punctuation mutation (comma -> period) -> no change (FAIL to mitigate).

Immediate takeaways:
- The anchor appears to bias open-ended continuation rather than directly inventing facts; when replaced with a real anchor, the model will lean on it.
- Sampling temperature plays a role: runs at 0.3 produce almost no hallucination; 0.7–0.9 amplify hallucination likelihood. Need to quantify slope.
- Reproducibility across seeds and small prompt perturbations is noisy; for a regression ticket we need an ensemble of seeds and fixed RNG snapshot where possible.

Regression reproduction checklist (for a ticket):
- Provide minimal prompt that reproduces the hallucination in <=200 tokens of generation (attached as repro-minimal.txt)
- Model name + variant + quantization + pool id
- Sampling params (temp, top_p, top_k if used), beam size if any
- Seed list and count (recommended 10 seeds)
- Runtime trace artifacts: token-level timestamps, kv-cache offsets (if available)
- Notes on whether Dedicated vs Hosted produced different outcomes

Hypotheses for root cause (ranked):
1) Kernel/quantization interaction: q4 variant may produce slightly smoother logits that push sampling toward high-prob but wrong sequences under high temp. (easy test: reproduce on a float32 dev instance)
2) Long-context positional bias: when certain trailing prompt tokens end with open-ended cues ("related work:" or colon) the model has a bias to invent citations to fill the slot. (test: change last punctuation and see distribution of named-entity tokens after colon)
3) Training data artifact: chain-of-thought style completions in pretraining that end with invented citations could create priors for younger models. (harder to test; rely on eval across model versions)

Next experiments to run (short):
- Grid over temp in [0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9] with 8 seeds each for the minimal repro prompt. Capture onset token and whether fabricated-citation appears.
- Same experiment but on float baseline (non-quantized) if possible.
- Automated mutator: implement script that slides a 12-token window across the prompt and logs halluc onset delta. Look for windows that reduce or increase onset consistently.

Short pseudo-commands (local repro):
- python repro/run_repro.py --model redwood-instruct-1.2-q4 --seed 3241 --temp 0.7 --prompt-file repro-minimal.txt --out trace/seed-3241.json
- bash scripts/mutate_window.sh repro-minimal.txt 70 81 neutral > mutated/neutral-70-81.txt

Open questions (to discuss with Rina/Maya):
- Should we throttle default temp for hosted endpoints for long-form QA paths? Tradeoff: creativity vs factual safety.
- Is the right mitigation at runtime (temperature, reranking) or at the prompt layer (context sanitization / canonicalization)?
- Can Console rule engine detect and flag likely "citation inventions" by scanning for named-entity + absent anchor in the prompt?

Notes to self (todo):
- Push a small PR with the grid experiment harness (ref PR: linked_artifacts entry above).
- Add a quick evaluation metric to nightly (fraction of eval cases with fabricated citations within first 200 tokens).
- Ask infra for temporary float32 repro machine (cc: maya).

Random scribbles / heuristics that might be helpful later:
- Look for patterns where invented citations almost always include surname-only + year format (e.g., "Zhou et al., 2020"). If so, add regex catch for surname-year patterns with no matching title in corpus.
- If onset latency correlates with presence of a colon or colon-like punctuation inside the last 40 tokens, flag the prompt as high-risk.
- For clients: consider offering a "conservative" generation mode (temp 0.2 + forced fact-check rerank) for sensitive QA routes.

End. Will iterate this into a proper ticket once we have grid numbers. Keeping messy notes here so I don't lose the crumbtrail idea.

-- Elliot
